title: What If Napoleon's Marshal Had Marched to the Guns?
topic: What if Napoleon's marshal had marched to the guns? (Waterloo, 18 June 1815)
mechanism: Sent on 17 June with over thirty thousand men to keep the beaten Prussians away, Grouchy kept to his orders when the guns of Waterloo were heard (at breakfast, the story goes, eating strawberries), chased a rear guard at Wavre while most Prussians marched west and broke Napoleon's flank; but most historians think even a win that day would not have saved Napoleon from the Austrian and Russian armies already marching on France.

beats.hook: Napoleon's best chance at Waterloo may have been sitting at breakfast eating strawberries: a slow push past a candlestick onto Grouchy's strawberry bowl while gunfire flickers in the window.
beats.but: Belgium, 18 June 1815: Napoleon on his grey before his columns, Wellington's red lines on the far ridge, the Prussians beaten two days earlier somewhere east.
beats.then: A day earlier Napoleon sent Grouchy and over thirty thousand men after the Prussians; rain all night, Napoleon waits for the mud to dry.
beats.conflict: Grouchy at breakfast; the rumble from the west; Gerard: 'Marshal, we must march to the guns!' Grouchy: 'My orders are to follow the Prussians.'
beats.pivot: Now, what if Grouchy had turned around? The sand table: the GROUCHY block turns toward WATERLOO while the hourglass runs out: TOO LATE? (some historians say he would have arrived too late anyway).
beats.so: So the strawberries probably didn't change the war: Austrian and Russian armies were already marching on France.
beats.closing: Just which village gave us 'meet your Waterloo': one strawberry on a wall, the village sign WATERLOO at sunset.
